old_title: Lossiemouth gives Mullins third winner at Punchestown, results from Ascot, Haydock and more - live
new_title: Grey Dawning wins at Haydock and Lossiemouth gives Mullins third winner at Punchestown: horse racing - as it happened
old_text:
Next in the betting list for the Betfair Chase is the hugely talented but slightly frustrating Jagwar, who went through last season without a win in four starts.
The last of those was an unseat in the Grand National, but he was also beaten just half-a-length in a red-hot Ultima at Cheltenham in March.
Dan Skelton's chaser is trading at around 11-10 to follow up last year's success, but faces an intriguing new opponent in Noel Meade's Affordale Fury, a steadily progressive chaser last year in top-class company until suffering an injury when fancied for the Irish Gold Cup in February.
His win in the Savills Chase at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting - with the dual Cheltenham Gold Cup winner, Galopin Des Champs, back in third - was the highlight.
Next up at Haydock is the feature event: the first Grade One of the new winter campaign in Britain, and and field of seven going to post headed by last year's winner, Grey Dawning.
Closely bunched in the early stages, as they go out on the first of two circuits ...
The Egyptian Ginge is front rank along with Hartington and Phantomofthepoints ...
They're all going well coming out of the back for the first time ...
Matty's Getaway is just last as they come up the straight but there's still only three lengths from first (The Egyptian Ginge) to last...
Seaniecon has made a little ground towards the lead, they're back out past the stands with six to jump. No significant mistakes so far.
Now Phantomofthepoinst starts to lose touch, The Egyptian Ginge still in front, Seaniecon ridden a little too now ...
Out of the back, three to jump, Matty's Getaway possibly going best ....
Now Matty's Getaway comes through to lead two out .. Supreme Malinas tries to reel him in, Seaniecon only third ...
Down to the last ... Matty's Getaway leads, Supreme Malinas getting closer all the time, they're fighting it out to the line, only a neck now .... but Matty's Getaway has just enough to get it done.
The top two in the market were both successful last time out. Matty's Getaway took a 10-runner race at Chepstow on 11 October, coming nearly 10 lengths clear at the finish on soft ground, while Seaniecon led home a 19-runner field at Cheltenham's October meeting.
It looks as though Matty's Getaway has lost a shoe on the way to post. He'll need to get that fixed before they can, er, get away.
There's a bit more for the punters to get stuck into in the next race at Haydock, a handicap hurdle over three miles, with nine runners going to post following the scratching of Yellow Car.
Matty's Getaway is the 100-30 market leader, with my fancy Seaniecon next in on 7-2 and Hartington on 4-1.
William Munny, the runner-up in the Supreme Novice Hurdle in 2025, is the only other runner in the four-strong field at a single-figure price. Barry Connell's gelding is 7-1, and it's 20-1 bar the two.
All eyes on the stunning setting of Punchestown in County Kildare now, as Lossiemouth, the champion over hurdles, makes her first start of the 2026-27 season in the Grade One Morgiana Hurdle.
She arrives with a career record of 15 wins from 19 starts including no fewer than 11 Grade One successes, and has finished second in three of her four defeats.
Freddie Gordon is talking to ITV Racing on the way back to unsaddle and suggests that Kocktail Bleu may now head over fences for a novice chasing campaign.
News arriving from Punchestown that the five-year-old Mighty Park was at the head of a 1-2-3 for Willie Mullins in the Beginners Chase.
He was ninth of 11 in last season's Supreme Novice Hurdle but looks made for chasing and will head to a sterner target at one of the big Christmas meetings in Ireland according to his trainer.
He has a super jump in him. I'd imagine Mighty Park will stay at around two miles. I don't think we'll be going up in trip yet, we don't need to."
The well-fancied Manganese - priced up at around 11-2 - has come out of the handicap hurdle that is next up at Haydock, and Kocktail Bleu is a very warm favourite at around 6-4.
Smokeringinthedark is next in on 5-2, it's 11-2 for Give It To Me Oj, and 10-1 bar the three.
Kingofthefrontier was giving weight to his field in the last race, but it will be level-weights in the Grade One Formby Novice Hurdle at Aintree on Boxing Day if, as seems likely, that's where he heads next. John Dawson is looking ahead in the winner's enclosure:
We're just feeling our way through. Our next plan would be the Formby. We just wanted to see if he was fast enough around here. He laid up nicely and as soon as Conor gave him a squeeze, he responded quickly.
The three-runner Ascot Hurdle is imminent at Ascot: the front-running Lucky Place is odds-on at around 4-7, and it's easy to see Nicky Henderson's gelding getting a very easy time of it on the lead.
A big, big win for John Dawson's North Yorkshire stable. They were off the mark at Grade Two level when Kingofthefrontier won at Cheltenham last month and now they have another, from a horse with the obvious potential to go on to even better things.
The winner definitely appreciated the fierce pace up front, which looked full-on from the off, and no sooner had Hold The Throw made his move between the final two than Kingofthefrontier appeared to swallow him up.
Four hurdles to jump, still Saint Jeannais leads, North Shore just outside ...
It's been a decent lick up front, they're turning out of the back and about to head up the long home straight ...
Three out - North Shore just in front over it, from Saint Jeannais ...
Hold The Throw is making ominous progress now ... Hold The Throw goes on between the last two, Kingofthefrontier in pursuit ...
Down to the last, now it's Kingofthefrontier in front, John Dawson's runner has a decent advantage up the run-in and he's going to go on for another big win for his small stable!
Well done to Jamie & Josh Moore, who have a Grade Two win to their names just a month after officially launching their training partnership.
We're off to Haydock shortly though, for the Grade Two Newton Novice Hurdle, where North Shore will set off as favourite at around 3-1.
He took at decent novice at Cheltenham's October meeting, by seven lengths, and is priced up at around 2-1 with Chris Gordon's Cosmic Connection next in on 100-30. He was a red-hot favourite for the Persian War Novice Hurdle at Chepstow on his return in early October but finished only ninth of the 11 runners.
Kingofthefrontier has been well-backed today too and is an 11-2 chance to follow up his win in the Grade Two Sharp Novice Hurdle at Cheltenham.
Blow Your Wad is the first to be ridden, Doyen Quest leads four out ...
Master Chewy now second, Blow Your Wad still ridden but not losing too much ground ..
Two out, Doyen Quest leads, Master Chewy ridden ...
Up to the last, Blow Your Wad staying on again, going to be close over the last ...
Doyen Quest and Blow Your Wad go head to head for the line ... Blow Your Wad is gaining by the stride ... edges ahead a few strides from the line and wins!
And as I was writing that last entry, Blow Your Wad actually edged in front of Master Chewy in the betting. It's a positive sign for the Moores' runner.
Heading towards post time for the first televised race from Ascot, and Master Chewy is a slightly uneasy favourite at around 13-8, with Blow Your Wad attracting a little cash to give Jamie & Josh Moore a first Grade Two win since they took over as the official training team at the Moore family operation in Sussex.
Leaving today's action to one side for a moment, the ever-popular former Champion Hurdle winner, Constitution Hill, seems likely to take the next step in his ongoing career on the Flat at Kempton Park in midweek.
Constitution Hill is entered for both the Unibet Floodlit Stakes at Kempton on Wednesday and the Midnite Churchill Stakes at Southwell on Friday, but the fact that Oisin Murphy is available to ride at the Sunbury track in midweek is likely to tip the balance.
"We have him in at Southwell," Nicky Henderson, Constitution Hill's trainer, says, "and it's almost exactly the same horses in there as Kempton, but Oisin is booked for Wednesday and I think we are all set for Kempton. Oisin can't do Friday, so I think we will go where he can go.
"Oisin and Ryan [Moore] have both won on him and they are two of the best jockeys in the world. They're all good but those two boys are exceptional and it's nice to have one of them on board."
Possible opponents for Constitution Hill on Wednesday include El Cordobes, from Charlie Appleby's stable in Newmarket, with the new champion jockey, Billy Loughnane, already booked to ride, and John & Thady Gosden's Warrant Holder, who is owned by the King & Queen.
The non-runners at Ascot are disappointing for racegoers, punters and the track alike, but from a betting perspective, the ITV Racing schedule has held up well. There are nine races in all, and just two have an odds-on favourite: the Ascot Hurdle at 1.30 and the Morgiana Hurdle in Ireland, where Lossiemouth was always going to be an exceptionally short price.
The first item on the menu for sofa-based punter's is the 1965 Chase at Ascot in around 20 minutes' time, when Master Chewy, from the in-form Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies stable, is going to set off at around 11-10 against Blow Your Wad (Jamie & Josh Moore) and Doyen Quest (Dan Skelton).
Like last week's valuable novice chase at Cheltenham, this is a race that started out with a "big two" and now has neither in the field. But Doyen Quest and BlowYourWad can both boast strong Grade Two form in last season's Oaksey Chase at Sandown in April, where the pair finished first and second.
Hello and welcome to the Guardian's liveblog coverage of the afternoon's racing action, featuring the Grade One Betfair Chase - the first of 38 Grade One events spread out over the next five months of the jumping campaign that will carry us into the depths of winter and then out the other side.
Never mind winter, though. Some proper autumn weather - rain, and lots of it - would be very welcome just now, as this afternoon's valuable card at Ascot is just the latest in recent weeks to suffer from a slew of non-runners due to the prevailing fast ground.
The going description was changed to good-to-firm, good in places at the Berkshire track earlier today, and in addition to the high-profile scratching of Lulamba from the Ladbrokes 1965 Chase at 12.55, Steel Ally, who replaced Lulamba at the top of the market, is now an absentee, too.
That leaves just three to go to post, and there are also just three in the Grade Two Ascot Hurdle at 1.30 in the absence of Altobelli. Half a dozen runners in two Grade Two events worth a total of £200k is a desperately poor showing, but there are at least no non-runners - as yet - in the seven-strong field for the Hurst Park Handicap Chase at 3.18.
But the Haydock card will undoubtedly be the focus of most punters' attention this afternoon, and the Betfair Chase promises to be fascinating as Grey Dawning, last year's winner, seeks to join the likes of Kauto Star, Cue Card and fellow-grey Bristol De Mai on the list of multiple winners.
The preceding stayers' handicap hurdle has the only double-figure field on the nine-race ITV Racing card, and there is a bonus trip too in mid-afternoon to Punchestown in County Kildare, where the ever-popular Lossiemouth, the reigning champion hurdler ...
... is due to make her seasonal debut in the Grade One Morgiana Hurdle at 2.10.
My picks for the ITV races are here, and we're off and running with the 1965 Chase at Ascot at 12.55.

GREY DAWNING WIN LAUNCHES HUGE CELEBRATIONS AT HAYDOCK
Grey Dawning, the 11-10 favourite, joined the illustrious list of dual winners of Betfair Chase at Haydock on Saturday, prompting a big Saturday crowd to sign the praises of Dan and Harry Skelton after a convincing defeat of Jagwar in the first Grade One event of the British season.
Harry Skelton, Grey Dawning's rider, was always perfectly positioned and travelling well against the rail as first Affordale Fury and then Jagwar led the field through the first two-and-a-half miles.
Skelton then made smooth progress to challenge Jagwar between the third- and second-last fences. Jagwar raised a second effort to jump alongside Grey Dawning at the last, but Skelton had more than enough in hand to go four-and-a-quarter lengths clear at the line.
A crowd packed half-a-dozeen deep around the paddock serenaded the winner with a chorus of "Walking in a Skelton Wonderland" as Skelton returned to unsaddle.
"This is very special," the rider said. "One day when I am not riding, I will always remember this place. Those are the memories you do it for. He was fantastic out there today and he never put a foot wrong."
Dan Skelton too was swept up by the atmosphere and reception for his grey chaser.
"It is great to be involved in such iconic horses and it is just an amazing achievement from the horse and a fabulous ride from Harry," Skelton said. "Harry is riding at the top of his game and he does more for me than you will ever appreciate, and it is a fantastic team effort."
Grey Dawning finished fourth in last season's CheltenhamGoldCup, beaten around 16 lengths behind Gaelic Warrior, and is expected to head instead to the RyanairChase, over two-and-a-half miles, at next year's festival meeting.
"The truth is we tried for a Gold Cup and we weren't quite good enough," Dan Skelton said. "The Ryanair is a Grade One, it is the marquee race on the Thursday and this horse is definitely better in a Ryanair than a Gold Cup and that's where he will go."
Grey Dawning can be backed at around 10-1 for the Ryanair Chase, in a market headed by Willie Mullins's Fact To File at around 5-1.

It's been a story of small fields all over today, but that was a cracking finish to the final race of the day at Haydock. And the crowd will be heading away into the Newton-le-Willows evening still buzzing after that hugely popular win for Grey Dawning, the favourite, in the Betfair Chase.
There's six horses going to post for the final ITV race at Haydock, Dexperts Opinion is heading hte market at 5-2, and Saladins Son is a 7-2 shot alongside Jaccours.
Dan Skelton is looking ahead to Grey Dawning's spring target, and it sounds very much as if he'll drop back to the intermediate trip of the Ryanair Chase having run fourth in the Gold Cup last season.
We tried for a Gold Cup and we weren't quite good enough. The Ryanair is a Grade One and it's the marquee race on the Thursday and all these races need supporting. This horse is definitely better in a Ryanair than a Gold Cup and that's where he'll go.
There'll be lots more to pick up from Haydock, but for now it's back to Ascot for the day's feature handicap chase: The Hurst Park Handicap Chase, with course-specialist Vanderpoel a very warm favourite to follow up a recent track-and-trip success at around 11-10.
I'm with another Skelton-trained runner though: the mare Shakeyatailfeather, who was only four-and-a-quarter lengths behind Vanverpoel at Ascot and gets plenty of weight here.
That was a supremely confident ride by Harry Skelton on Grey Dawning, he probably did not want to be in front as soon as he was but when Jagwar tried to make a fight of it after the last, there was more than enough left in the tank to put the race to bed.
Jagwar deserves plenty of credit too - racing up with the pace seemed to bring a new, more polished jumper to the fore. Affordale Fury was perhaps a little bit below his best, but had been off the track for a long time and made a few minor errors which added up in the end.
Affordale Fury straight into the lead, looks like a solid pace ...
Out into the back, closely grouped, Handstands brings up the rear.
Affordale Fury was a bit slow over the third, Grey Dawning settled on the inside.
Jagwar is alongside Affordale Fury over the next ... All jumping well down the back, though Gorgeous Tom has lost a little ground.
Salver sits fourth, Konfusion is a little outpaced along with Gorgeous Tom.
Down the straight, now Jagwar leads by a length from Affordale Fury, he's been jumping very well so far but does have a habit of throwing in the odd mistake.
Going past the stands, a circuit to run. Jagwar leads, Affordale Fury next, Grey Dawning and Salver next and its five lengths back to the rest.
Down the back, Grey Dawning's backers will be on good terms with themselves as the favourite goes well.
Affordale Fury is still there but has made a couple of minor errors, Jagwar leads them out of the back.
Turning in ... still Jagwar from Grey Dawning and Affordale Fury ...
Grey Dawning is cruising in behind, at the last ditch and now Grey Dawning is into the lead ..
Jagwar back with him at the second-last, and they're alongside at the last too ...
Jagwar is briefly in front ... but now Grey Dawning finds more, he's got plenty left to give and the favourite is going to notch a second Betfair Chase win ...
My feeling about this race is that Affordale Fury could give Grey Dawning plenty to think about, not least as the unusually quick ground for Haydock at this time of year will suit his front-running style.
No end of other, alternative scenarios exist, however.

He had a pipe-opener on the Flat at Nottingham earlier this month, but was a decent third in Grade One novice company at Aintree on his most recent start over fences.

Hello and welcome to the Guardian's liveblog coverage of the afternoon's racing action, featuring the Grade One Betfair Chase - the first of 38 Grade One events spread out over the next five months of the jumping campaign that will carry us into the depths of winter and then out the other side.
